_meta.indication: GILENYA is indicated for the treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) to reduce the frequency of clinical exacerbations and to delay the accumulation of physical disability.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal efficacy and safety trial
pivotal_trials.design: 2-year randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients with RRMS
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS); median age 37 years, median disease duration 6.7 years, median baseline EDSS 2.0
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized relapse rate 0.18 (GILENYA 0.5 mg) vs 0.40 (placebo), p<0.001; 70% vs 46% of patients relapse-free (p<0.001); hazard ratio of disability progression 0.70 (95% CI 0.52, 0.96), p=0.02

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 pivotal efficacy and safety trial
pivotal_trials.design: 1-year randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (vs interferon beta-1a) study in RRMS patients
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS); median age 36 years, median disease duration 5.9 years, median baseline EDSS 2.0
pivotal_trials.n: Patients randomized to GILENYA 0.5 mg (n=431), 1.25 mg (n=426), or interferon beta-1a IM 30 micrograms weekly (n=435)
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized relapse rate 0.16 (GILENYA 0.5 mg) vs 0.33 (interferon beta-1a), p<0.001; 83% vs 70% relapse-free (p<0.001); hazard ratio of disability progression 0.71 (95% CI 0.42, 1.21), p=0.21

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥10% and > placebo): headache (25% vs 23%), influenza, diarrhea (12% vs 7%), back pain (12% vs 7%), liver transaminase elevations (ALT/AST increased 14% vs 5%), and cough (10% vs 8%). Bradycardia (4% vs 1%) occurs at treatment initiation.
target_moa: Fingolimod is metabolized to the active metabolite fingolimod-phosphate, a sphingosine 1-phosphate receptor modulator that binds S1P receptors 1, 3, 4 and 5 and blocks the capacity of lymphocytes to egress from lymph nodes, reducing peripheral blood lymphocytes.
modality: Small molecule (orally active sphingosine 1-phosphate receptor modulator)

rems.type: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of bradyarrhythmia and atrioventricular block at treatment initiation, infections, macular edema, respiratory effects, hepatic effects, and fetal risk.

advisory_committee.vote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee voted unanimously that there was substantial evidence of effectiveness in reducing relapses in RRMS, voted 24-1 for substantial evidence in delaying accumulation of physical disability, and voted unanimously that the safety data for 0.5 mg daily justified approval.

summary.text: As the first oral MS treatment NDA, Gilenya was granted Fast Track status (IND fast track June 7, 2007) and priority review (February 18, 2010), was discussed at the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee (June 10, 2010), and was approved with a REMS; it was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Because Gilenya is the first NDA for an oral treatment for MS to be submitted, it was granted Fast Track status and was given a priority review designation.
The IND was granted fast track designation in June 7, 2007.
The application was granted priority review on February 18, 2010.
This application was discussed at the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee Meeting on June 10, 2010.

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for GILENYA (fingolimod) to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of bradyarrhythmia and atrioventricular block at treatment initiation, infections, macular edema, respiratory effects, hepatic effects, and fetal risk.

requirement.text: 1679-1: Deferred pediatric study under PREA — a 24-month, randomized, active-controlled study evaluating pharmacokinetics, safety and efficacy of fingolimod vs interferon beta-1a IM (Avonex) in relapsing-remitting MS.

citations.quote: 1679-1: Deferred pediatric study under PREA: a 24-month, randomized, active-controlled, parallel group study to evaluate the single and multiple dose pharmacokinetics of fingolimod, and the safety and efficacy of multiple doses of fingolimod compared to interferon beta 1-a-intramuscular (Avonex) for the treatment of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.

requirement.text: 1679-2: A postmarketing observational prospective, parallel cohort study in relapsing MS patients to assess potentially serious risks including eye toxicity, cardiac/vascular toxicity, pulmonary toxicity, seizures, serious/opportunistic infections, malignancies, liver toxicity and atypical MS relapse.

citations.quote: 1679-2: A postmarketing observational prospective, parallel cohort study in relapsing multiple sclerosis patients to assess the potentially serious risk of: eye toxicity, cardiac and vascular toxicity, pulmonary toxicity, seizures, serious and opportunistic infections, malignancies, liver toxicity and atypical multiple sclerosis relapse.

requirement.text: 1679-3: Develop and maintain a prospective, observational pregnancy exposure registry in the US comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to fingolimod during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 1679-3: Develop and maintain a prospective, observational pregnancy exposure registry study conducted in the United States that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to fingolimod during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.
